discovery: Discovery of neutron halo nuclei at the limits of nuclear stability

nominees.name: Isao Tanihata
nominees.affiliation: RCNP, Osaka University, Japan / Beihang University, China

motivation: In 1985 Isao Tanihata and collaborators used radioactive beams to measure interaction cross sections of light neutron-rich isotopes and found the anomalously large matter radius of 11Li. Björn Jonson, with the late P. G. Hansen, identified the physical explanation: a neutron halo, in which weakly bound neutrons tunnel far beyond the core. Jonson's ISOLDE and GSI experiments on momentum distributions and Coulomb dissociation then established halos and Borromean three-body systems as a new form of nuclear matter. The discovery overturned the textbook picture of nuclei as compact, constant-density drops with radii scaling as A^(1/3). It launched the worldwide programme of radioactive-beam facilities (RIKEN RIBF, FRIB, FAIR) and made drip-line nuclei the key testing ground for modern theory, from effective field theories of halos to ab initio predictions with chiral forces. Few discoveries have reshaped nuclear structure physics so deeply.
